match.reason: None of the bank points teaches how government responds to changing indicators; the closest, Economic indicators, only classifies indicators as leading, coincident or lagging, and the business cards cover business performance rather than government action.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Remember, other: "Indicators show a problem" goes beyond the card, which says indicators show how the economy is doing. Indicators do not always show a problem, so this could mislead. Something like "Indicators show how the economy is doing, and the government can respond to the one that has changed" fits the card better.

rejected.title: Responding to indicators
card: An economic indicator is a measure that shows how the economy is doing. Examples are the unemployment rate, the inflation rate and the growth rate of GDP.
The government watches these indicators. When one moves away from what it wants, it may act to move it back.
If unemployment rises, the government can fund apprenticeships and training places. This helps people gain skills and find work.
The action is matched to the indicator that has changed. A rise in unemployment calls for a different response from a rise in prices.
rejected.remember: Indicators show a problem, and the government can respond to the one that has changed.

a.q: Why might the government fund more training places when unemployment rises?
opts: To help jobseekers gain skills and find work
To make prices across the economy stay stable
To raise the amount of tax people must pay
To lower the number of people who want a job
a.why: Rising unemployment means more people are without work, and training builds skills that help them get jobs. It does not target prices, which is a different indicator. It also does not change how many people want work.
a.clue: Which indicator changed, and what would help that group?

b.q: Suppose the unemployment rate in Australia rises from 4% to 5%. Which response matches this indicator?
opts: Funding more apprenticeships and training places
Cutting the number of training places on offer
Acting to keep prices across the economy stable
Waiting until the inflation rate changes as well
b.why: Unemployment has risen, so a matching response helps people gain skills and find work, such as funding apprenticeships and training places. Acting on prices is tempting, but it responds to a different indicator. Cutting training places would work against the aim.
b.clue: Match the response to the indicator that moved.

a.q: Why might the government fund more training places when unemployment rises?
opts: To help jobseekers gain skills and find work
To make prices across the economy stay stable
To raise the amount of tax people must pay
To lower the number of people who want a job
a.why: Rising unemployment means more people are without work, and training builds skills that help them get jobs. It does not target prices, which is a different indicator. It also does not change how many people want work.
a.clue: Which indicator changed, and what would help that group?

b.q: Last year, the unemployment rate in Australia rose from 4% to 5%. Which response matches this indicator?
opts: Funding more apprenticeships in a regional town
Ignoring the change because it is only one point
Cutting back on training places in all trades
Waiting for the inflation rate to change as well
b.why: Unemployment has risen, so the government can act on it by funding apprenticeships that help people into work. Cutting training places would work against the aim. Waiting for a different indicator does not respond to the one that has changed.
b.clue: Pick the action that helps people find work.

a.best: To help jobseekers gain skills and find work

b.best: Funding more apprenticeships in a regional town

problems.detail: The stem says as fact that 'Last year, the unemployment rate in Australia rose from 4% to 5%'. That is not accurate for recent years, when Australia's rate stayed around 3.5–4.5%, and it will date. Frame it as a hypothetical (e.g. 'Suppose the unemployment rate rises from 4% to 5%').
The clue 'Pick the action that helps people find work' points straight to the apprenticeships option, so it gives the answer away instead of prompting thinking.

The right option adds the narrow detail 'in a regional town' to a national rise in unemployment. This can confuse students about whether a local action matches a national indicator. 'Funding more apprenticeships and training places' would be clearer.

check.summary: The card and question a are sound. Question b presents a made-up unemployment rise in Australia as a real fact from last year, and its clue gives away the answer, so both should be fixed.
